name: Sierra Leonean Cassava Leaf Plasas
description: Cassava leaf plasas is genuinely considered Sierra Leone's national dish - unlike jollof, where palm oil is just an accent, plasas is real palm-oil-forward, the oil acting as the actual backbone that carries the smoked fish and peanut through the whole pot. Real technique loosens the peanut paste with hot broth before stirring it in, and the dish traditionally simmers for two hours or more until it collapses into a thick, dark, silky stew - not a quick 15-minute finish.

ingredients_full.note: standing in for pounded cassava leaves

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

ingredients.note: standing in for pounded cassava leaves

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

steps_detailed: Simmer the beef with the onion, jalapeño, bouillon, and enough water to cover, 25-30 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the palm oil - real technique treats this as the backbone of the dish, not an accent - and let it warm through, 3-4 minutes.
Add the smoked fish and simmer 5 minutes so the oil takes on its smoky flavor.
Loosen the peanut butter with a few spoonfuls of the hot broth first, then stir it into the pot.
Add the spinach and simmer at least 30-40 minutes, longer if you have time, until the greens collapse into a thick, dark, silky stew.

name: Sierra Leonean Groundnut Stew
description: Groundnut stew, built on real ground peanuts, is a beloved Sierra Leonean dish often served alongside cassava leaf plasas, real technique whisking the peanut butter slowly for a smooth broth.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter slowly with the tomatoes, jalapeño, and a little water, add to the pot.
Simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Sierra Leonean Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice, part of the wider West African jollof tradition, real technique frying the blended tomato-pepper base down until it deepens - here palm oil is used more sparingly than in plasas, as an accent rather than the backbone.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, jalapeño, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the puree and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes until deeply reduced.
Stir in the rice, broth, and chicken, cover, and cook on low 20-25 minutes until tender.

name: Sierra Leonean Potato Leaf Plasas
description: Potato leaf plasas is real technique different from cassava leaf plasas - the leaves go in after the meat, cooking for less time, which is what keeps them with a real chewy, al dente texture rather than fully collapsing.

Stir in the palm oil and peanut butter, and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Add the spinach last and simmer only 8-10 minutes more - real technique keeps this shorter than cassava leaf plasas, so the leaves stay a little chewy rather than fully breaking down.

name: Sierra Leonean Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, is the traditional accompaniment to plasas, real technique pounding until completely smooth and elastic.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Drain and pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy, free of lumps.
steps: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.

name: Sierra Leonean Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish, a beloved Sierra Leonean street food especially along Lumley Beach, real technique keeping the seasoning simple to let the smoky char carry the flavor.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Sierra Leonean Ginger Beer
description: Spicy ginger beer, a beloved non-alcoholic beverage, real technique steeping fresh ginger long enough for its real heat to come through.
steps_detailed: Steep the grated ginger in 2 cups hot water for 20 minutes.
Strain, then stir in the sugar and lemon juice, and chill before serving over ice.

name: Sierra Leonean Peanut Sauce
description: A simple ground-peanut sauce base, echoing the flavor of plasas and groundnut stew, used across many Sierra Leonean dishes.
steps_detailed: Whisk the peanut butter slowly with 1 cup water and the tomatoes into a smooth sauce.
Simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
